text:
jordan: Heads up — prepping a small RFC for region failover behavior for the API gateway. TL;DR: introduce a 'failover slice' concept + header attribute scheme to let clients / console opt into deterministic fallback stacks instead of "any available region". want quick sanity-checks.

sophie: Love the idea of explicit slices. Does this mean we add another routing dimension (route.slice) that maps to a list of region groups? :thinking:

kevin: Yep. We currently have prefer-local -> then cost fallback. Problem is it's too fuzzy for enterprise customers who need deterministic egress. Slice approach lets them pin a prioritized set: primary slice (local), warm-standby slice (same continent but cheaper), remote slice (global).

aj: Sketch of how the header override could look: `X-RW-Failover-Slice: warm-standby` and `X-RW-Region-Hint: eu-west-1`. Gateway honors header if caller has permission. Also console UX can set per-route defaults.

maria: Important: authz check on header overrides. We can't let self-serve customers force traffic to lower-SLA regions without approval. Also telemetry needs to tag decisions: `routing.slice.chosen`, `routing.slice.fallback_count`.

kevin: Agreed. We should emit metrics: `route.slice.requests`, `route.slice.latency_p95`, `route.slice.failover_rate`, and a counter for header-overrides-used. This will power the console breakdowns.

rami: Implementation note: the routing graph currently resolves region by two signals: client geo + route config. We add `slice` as a third signal with precedence ordering: header -> route-level slice -> route default policy. Also hedging: if latency probe to primary crosses threshold, we can speculative-hedge to second slice.

aj: Example policy snippet (proto-yaml):
```
route: /v1/generate/*
  match: prefix
  slice_policy:
    default: primary
    slices:
      primary:
        regions: [eu-west-1]
        weight: 0.9
      warm-standby:
        regions: [eu-central-1, eu-west-3]
        weight: 0.09
      remote:
        regions: [us-west-2]
        weight: 0.01
  header_overrides:
    allowed_headers: [X-RW-Region-Hint, X-RW-Failover-Slice]
    require_role: routing_override
  hedging:
    p95_threshold_ms: 300
    speculative_to: warm-standby
```

tess: For rollout UX: Console should show the effective slice (per route) and allow toggling a canary percent to a different slice. e.g., '5% to warm-standby for 24h'. Need audit log entries when someone changes allowed_headers.

maria: Also consider a read-only lineage header in responses: `X-RW-Routed-Region` and `X-RW-Routed-Slice` for troubleshooting. Those can be scrubbed for PII-sensitive customers though.

kevin: On failover semantics: if all regions in a slice are unhealthy, we should skip to next slice rather than pick randomly. That preserves determinism. But we also need a graceful degrade policy: if target slice is healthy but overloaded, we can route with reduced concurrency (throttling) instead of immediate failover.

jordan: Good call. Suggest adding `slice_state: [healthy, degraded, offline]` and an SLO-driven threshold to move states. Telemetry should expose `slice_state_changes` and time-in-state percentiles.

deploy-bot: deploy: routing-config-service@staging started a canary deployment (id: canary-2025-04-11-3). Logs: 2/5 replicas upgraded.

rami: Regarding hedging: be careful with token-cost explosion. If we speculative-call a second region, we must cancel early if p50 of primary completes. Add a max-additional-tokens budget per request.

aj: Good point. Maybe hedging only for short responses (max tokens <= 512) and only when latency SLO risk is high. Also add a per-customer hedging quota.

tess: UX: can we show historical failover trace in the request inspector? e.g., timeline: start -> routed to eu-west-1 -> p95 probe missed -> hedged to eu-central-1 -> response from eu-central-1. Makes postmortem for customer easy.

maria: For authz: add RBAC rule `routing.override.headers` and treat that as an enterprise-only feature behind a feature flag. Default behavior remains route-level slices only.

jordan: Nice. Action items I hear: 1) I will draft RFC w/ policy proto example + telemetry fields. 2) @kevin + rami to design metric names and alerting thresholds (slice failover rate > 0.5% -> investigate). 3) @aj to prototype header auth checks in gateway. 4) @tess to mock console UX for per-route slice canary + request inspector. 5) @maria will write RBAC proposal.

kevin: Small nit: thresholds should be based on baseline per-route p95, not a flat 300ms. i.e., delta over baseline. Otherwise tiny routes get weird behavior.

jordan: Agreed — make threshold relative. Will capture in RFC.

maria: Also add a feature flag that turns on response lineage headers only for internal orgs.

aj: I'll add unit tests around header precedence and a property test that ensures deterministic fallback ordering.

tess: I'll wire up a dashboard mock with drilldowns: slice selection, slice latency, hedged request rate, header-overrides-used.

jordan: Thanks all — I'll drop the RFC link here when ready. planning to canary the gateway changes in staging next Tue. :rocket:
